data.gender_notes: Vishnudev is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God in the form of Vishnu
data.long_meaning: The name Vishnudev is derived from the Sanskrit words Vishnu, meaning god, and Dev, meaning god or divine. Vishnudev is a name for the Hindu deity Vishnu, who is the preserver in the Hindu trinity. He is the protector and sustainer of the universe, and the embodiment of love, compassion, and purity. The name Vishnudev carries the meaning “God in the form of Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vishnudev usually hope their child will grow to embody god in the form of vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for the Hindu deity Vishnu, symbolizing divine protection, love, compassion, and purity.
data.etymology: Vishnudev belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God in the form of Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishnudev total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vishnudev holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is used to invoke and revere the Hindu god Vishnu. Vishnudev is often considered as the preserver of dharma (duty, law, and morality) and the symbol of love, compassion, and divine protection. The name Vishnudev is chanted in religious ceremonies, recitals, and mantras to seek his blessings and to maintain harmony and balance in life.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Vishnudev represents the ultimate power and compassion of the divine. It is believed that invoking the name Vishnudev can help purify one's mind, body, and soul, and bring an inner sense of peace and tranquility. The name Vishnudev is also considered as a reminder of the divine presence in all aspects of life, and inspires devotion, selflessness, and loving-kindness towards others.
